finding: Cross-repo dependency has no typed edge: blocked-by is {same-carrier item-id | decision | evidence | NONE}, and a foreign id is a dangling_reference_item refusal (:542). In a 14-repo system with one shared plugin (R15), every consumer repo depends on plugin items; that dependency can only be a prose evidence-blocker that never auto-clears. Observed this session: cf-337 depends on lc-64 across repos, expressed as prose, will not auto-return to NEW when lc-64 lands.
basis: modelled — read at design eceda8c :153-157 (blocked-by types), :542 (dangling_reference_item), R15 :66; and the live cf-337/lc-64 instance booked this session
disposition: mechanism — ready-to-land lc-66 (typed cross-repo edge blocked-by <repo>:<id>)

finding: The operator decision-queue has no aging, ranking, or cross-repo roll-up. decision <q> blockers route to the operator's queue (:155-156); R3 forbids a disposition that is 'the operator remembers', yet the decision queue IS exactly that, unbounded across 14 repos, and it is not a declared kind with growth control (R22 declares growth per kind; the queue is a view over blocked items, not a kind). Directly against the cheap-oversight intent.
basis: modelled — read at eceda8c :155-156, R3 :54, R22 :72; no kind row covers the decision queue in R20's list
disposition: mechanism — ready-to-land lc-67 (the decision queue as a declared kind with a flow alarm + cross-repo roll-up)

finding: R20's registered-kind list (items, done bodies, directives, audits, lanes, workflows, worktrees, lane branches, plugin cache) omits any cross-repo or coordination artifact, so 'a kind with no declared lifecycle is a router finding' cannot reach cross-repo dependency — it is not conceived as a kind at all. The structural root of F1.
disposition: prose-rest — folds into the close-class structural cure (lc-66)

finding: Detector home is single-repo ('a detector registers its home repo', §3.5), so a condition spanning repos — consumer X's item depends on plugin item Y now DONE; X should re-open — has no single home and no detector can own it. F1's enforcement half: cross-repo dependency cannot even be mechanically noticed.
disposition: prose-rest — folds into the close-class (a cross-repo detector home, lc-66)

finding: No cross-repo finding roll-up for cheap oversight: §3.4 notification is per-detector, counts-only, one-per-batch, local channel; nothing aggregates 'N repos hold parked findings / pending decisions' across the 14. Cheap oversight over a 14-repo system needs a roll-up the design does not name.
disposition: prose-rest — folds into lc-67 (the cross-repo roll-up is the decision-queue's view)

finding: Conservation checks COUNT and source blob-sha, not body content: R8's conservation is N-in=N-out, migrate records the source blob sha (cf-324). A migrated body GARBLED while the count holds passes clean — paraphrase-drift in a conservation costume. 'Nothing lost' is verified as 'nothing lost by count'.
basis: modelled — read at eceda8c R8 :59 and the migrate blob-sha rule (cf-324, ledger)
disposition: mechanism — ready-to-land lc-68 (per-body content hash across the migration boundary, not only the count)

finding: The dropped reference tier (§3.3: 'no reference tier, no dev-book concept survives; what fits none of law/workflow/journal/audit is dropped') leaves cross-cutting REASONING — the 'why this shape' that justifies a SET of laws, not one — with no home. Deliberate operator decision 2026-08-26; worth re-confirming now that a concrete instance (this design's own rationale) exists.
disposition: prose-rest — operator re-confirm; ready-to-land as a decision blocker on lc-69

finding: CROSS-ROW CLASS: the kind/vocabulary system is single-repo AND domain-scoped, so any cross-repo or cross-domain NECESSITY (a dependency, a coordination condition, a pending decision, an aggregate view) has no first-class slot and falls to prose the roll-up never sees. This is the exact shape of the tend gap one axis over — tend cured the domain-scope half (repo-self-work), the cross-repo half is untouched. One structural cure — a coordination layer: typed cross-repo edge (F1) + cross-repo detector home (F8) + cross-repo roll-up/decision-queue view (F3/F4) + coordination as a declared kind (F7) — outranks patching each row. Most aligned with the operator's stated intent that cross-repo coordination be first-class.
basis: modelled — cross-row read over the five vocabulary-slot rows at eceda8c
disposition: mechanism — the class is booked as lc-66 (the coordination layer); F3 roll-up as lc-67; the rest fold in
